text:
Jordan (AE): Kicking off a POC with MeridianCare. They want a 2h soak: sustained 620 qps, avg output ~384 tokens, p99 <170ms, errors <0.5%. Need run plan, sizing, and a quick per-hour cost delta for adding burst nodes + multi-AZ. Also they asked for encrypted KMS flow in our SOC answers. Can SE/SRE + Solutions triage?
Samira (SE): On it. Two quicks: what percent streaming vs full-response and how many prompts are templated (cacheable)?
Jordan (AE): ~58% streaming, ~42% repeatable templates (good KV cache potential). They prefer 13b quality but are price-sensitive; curious about a new 9b variant if we can show cost/latency wins.
Samira (SE): Proposed test: warmup 12m, ramp 8m to 620 qps, steady 2h, 10m cool-down. Arrival profile: Poisson + random microbursts (4% windows spike 3x for 30s). Models to test: rwd-9b-q4 (latency/cost trade), rwd-13b-q4 (quality), rwd-7b-q8 (fallback). KV prefix caching enabled. Keep streaming on for first-token flush. Suggest max_batch_delay 6ms for latency route; can relax to 10ms for cost runs.
Samira (SE): sample load command:
```
rwd-load --model rwd-9b-q4 --target-qps 620 --duration 7800 --ramp 480 --warmup 720 --burst-profile "random:4%:30s@3x" --concurrency 92 --payload-dist meridian_prompts.json
```
Mateo (SRE): Infra rec: Dedicated pool sized for 744 qps (+20% headroom). Autoscale min=1 max=3 nodes, cooldown 90s. Multi-AZ recommended. Fallback policy: 13b->9b->7b? Actually prefer 9b as intermediary between 13b and 7b. Pre-warm KV during ramp to avoid cold-miss tail. Recommend enabling autoscale buffer to pre-spin a node ~60s before expected large burst windows if we know schedule.
Lina (Solutions): Pricing quickballpark: Dedicated pool for rwd-9b-q4 to sustain 620 qps ~ $1,350/hr. For the 2h run + warmup/cooldown estimate ~ $3.2k. Burst-ready option (extra node reserved) adds ~+20% hourly. Hosted token-backup pricing ~ $0.19 / 1k inferred tokens as a rough fallback. I'll prepare two lines: baseline and burst-ready; will also include KMS/HSM notes for SOC.
load-bot: quick smoke run (internal):
```json
{"test":"meridian-smoke-2026-06-12","target_qps":620,"sustained_qps":618,"p50_ms":39,"p95_ms":108,"p99_ms":178,"error_rate_pct":0.4,"gpu_util_pct":83,"notes":"p99 178ms >170ms target. Options: bump +18% capacity, reduce max_batch_delay to 5ms, or try rwd-7b-q8 fallback for tight latency."}
```
Samira (SE): p99 178ms — close but above SLO. Fastest mitigation: spin +18% capacity then run a 30-45m validation. If still over, lower batch_delay to 5ms for the latency route. Which infra option is quickest?
Mateo (SRE): Spinning +18% is fastest. I'll provision nodes now and schedule a 45m validation in ~50m. Will also enable KV pre-population during ramp. If validation still misses, we'll try batch_delay -> 5ms.
Samira (SE): I'll stage the config change to lower batch_delay as a quick flip. Also will run a short quality check on rwd-9b->7b fallback to ensure MeridianCare's quality bar stays acceptable.
Lina (Solutions): Updating pricing with two options: (A) baseline (B) burst-ready (+20% capacity) and I'll document KMS flow for the SOC questionnaire (KMS + HSM for key wrapping, customer-managed keys supported in Private). Will DM redacted SOC snippets.
load-bot: 45m validation after +18% capacity:
```json
{"test":"meridian-val-2026-06-12","target_qps":620,"sustained_qps":621,"p50_ms":36,"p95_ms":96,"p99_ms":166,"error_rate_pct":0.3,"gpu_util_pct":76,"notes":"p99 166ms meets <170ms SLO with +18% pool and KV pre-warm. Recommend final 2h soak with same config and monitoring for KV hit-rate and streaming ratio."}
```
Jordan (AE): Nice  that's within acceptance. Customer criteria: sustained 620 qps for 2h, p99 <170ms, errors <0.5%. I'll present baseline vs burst-ready pricing and the SOC/KMS notes. Scheduling the customer soak for next Tue. Thanks team! :party_parrot:
